steps.npc: I'm exploring the region for the good of the gnome people.

steps.player: You're not tracking down huge beasts to kill - you look equipped for it.

steps.npc: Well, if I find anything interesting I'll try and bring it back to the King. That might include animals, I suppose. I'd rather not kill it, though - most animals are more useful alive.

steps.player: How would you get it home, then?

steps.npc: Never underestimate the ingenuity of a gnome, friend.

steps.player: Have you found anything else interesting around here?

steps.npc: I've heard strange rumours about something the locals call the Broodoo. I haven't quite worked out what they are but they seem to be some sort of undead whose ghastly fate depends on the way they were killed.
I think they may be sacrifice victims - but I'm not sure why they are sacrificed. Either way the locals seem to be very scared of them.

options.text: What does this mint cake do?
options.condition: If the player has a Mint cake

steps.player: What does this mint cake do?

steps.npc: Gnomish mint cake is a great source of energy for the gnome traveller. It will give you that extra bit of zip when you are running out of steam.

steps.player: Ooh, that might come in very handy. Do you have any spare?

steps.npc: I need all the mint cake I have, I'm afraid.

options.text: What does this seed pod do?
options.condition: If the player has a Grand seed pod

steps.player: What does this seed pod do?

steps.npc: Ah, the seed pod of the Grand Tree is a fascinating spirit artefact. It is a very useful thing, though one must treat it with respect, since the Grand Tree has a connection with all of its parts, however distant they
may be. How do you think the Spirit Trees work?

If you launch its seeds in a far flung location, you will be helping the tree survive, so the grand tree will help a gnome glider pilot find you, using the seed burst itself (which marks the sky) and a little magic, and bring you
back home as an act of gratitude. Budding farmers will also find their link with plants to be just a little bit better than before.
However, it takes time for a pilot to find you, and if you are in a real hurry, and I mean a real emergency, you can just squash the seed pod. The Grand Tree doesn't like this, but will pull you back

home straight away. Don't do this if you need to do anything with plants straight away, though - your fingers will be considerably less green for a while after using the seed pod this way, and the journey is not

gnome-restaurant-dialogue.text: If the player doesn't have the correct item in their inventory:

steps.text: Although you have found your customer you don't appear to have brought the correct food with you! You need [a/some] [ordered gnome food/drink item]!

gnome-restaurant-dialogue.text: If the player has a premade item in their inventory:

steps.text: Premade dishes will not do I'm afraid. Only hand made Gnome Cuisine is good enough for customers of Aluft Aloft.

gnome-restaurant-dialogue.text: If the player has the correct item in their inventory:

steps.text: You hand over your delivery of [a/some] [ordered gnome food item] to Penwie.

steps.npc: At last a taste of home!

steps.text: If the reward is a mint cake:

steps.npc: Now that I have some proper food, I won't need this any more.

steps.text: You are given some mintcake as a tip.
If the reward is grand seed pods:

steps.npc: Here, take these Grand Seed pods. Very useful in emergencies!

steps.text: You are given some seed pods as a tip.
If the reward is a raw oomlie:

steps.npc: I traded with some of the locals for this - maybe you'll find it useful.

steps.text: You are given some raw oomlie bird meat as a tip.
If the reward is anything else:

steps.npc: You must have had to travel a long way to get this to me. Here's a little something extra as a tip.
